consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning is the visible outward product (character, virtues, good works) of a person's inner spiritual condition—especially the fruit of the Spirit—serving as the evidence by which individuals, teachers, or trees are known and judged (Gal 5:22-23, Matt 7:15-20, John 15, etc.). Alternatives (converts, offspring, praise, consequences, firstfruits) are acknowledged but secondary.
book_summary: Fruit is identified as a nation's works, by which it is judged, illustrated by the good tree bringing forth good fruit and by the kingdom given to a nation that brings forth the fruits thereof.
consensus_core_identification: outward works/character/produce evidencing inner (personal) spiritual condition, by which the agent is known or judged
book_core_identification: a nation's works by which it is judged
boundary_disagreement: Consensus applies the symbol primarily to individuals (believers, prophets, personal character and Spirit-produced virtues); the book restricts the referent to the works of nations under corporate judgment.
material_contradiction: None; both treat fruit as works that serve as the criterion of judgment drawn from the same Matthean tree imagery, without mutual exclusion.
rationale: Both cores reduce to works/produce that function as the basis of judgment. The book preserves that category and the supporting tree-fruit principle but materially narrows the agent from the consensus's dominant personal/individual cases to nations alone. This is a boundary refinement (BOOK_NARROWS / BOOK_SUBSET), not a replacement of the central referent or a contradiction. Matt 21:43 supplies the national case while Matt 7:17 supplies the general principle; personal applications remain compatible and unaddressed rather than denied.
strongest_objection: The settled consensus primary (fruit of the Spirit, personal character known by works) is far more prominent across traditions and the bulk of NT usage than the book's specific national restriction; the entry may over-weight a secondary corporate application.
